interpretation: Not a ranking. Absent/unlocated means not established in the cited inspected sources. Survey pins and measurement pins are separate. Differentiation refers to physical model parameters unless stated otherwise.

records.physics: Equilibrium second-order Jeans; tracer and halo components; spherical anisotropy profiles or constant cylindrical beta_z; current axisymmetric tracer has no self-gravity.
records.observables: Projected LOS second moments; Gaussian individual-velocity likelihood with measurement errors.
records.freedom: Spherical Plummer and classical additional tracers, NFW/Zhao halo and several anisotropy laws; axisymmetric Plummer + Zhao with flattening and inclination.
records.solver: Direct fixed quadrature (and classical adaptive reference routes); no trained surrogate.
records.differentiation: Physical-parameter autodiff through supported JAX forward/likelihood paths. NumPy J/D factors are postprocessing; analytic Zhao incomplete-beta shape derivatives are unsupported.
records.hardware: NumPy/SciPy CPU; JAX CPU/GPU, precision explicitly configured.
records.inference: emcee and NumPyro wrappers; persisted analysis identity, samples and restart.
records.public_status: Public BSD-3-Clause repository; alpha package and development source differ.
records.comparison_scope: Matched spherical and axisymmetric forward/likelihood tests; native examples and conditional coverage separately.

records.geometry: Axisymmetric public solver uses spherical alignment
records.physics: Spectral solution of the two-dimensional Jeans boundary problem with general beta(r, theta). The public cylindrical-alignment solver was removed in v9.
records.observables: Intrinsic/projected first and second moments, including PMs, PSF and aperture treatment.
records.freedom: Projected tracer requires MGE; potential may be MGE or a callable. Intrinsic solver accepts general density/potential callables and anisotropy.
records.solver: Direct spectral method in log radius, finite domain with outer Robin condition; line-of-sight integration remains for projection.
records.differentiation: spectral_derivs computes spatial density/potential derivatives, not automatic derivatives with respect to physical model parameters. Inspected implementation uses NumPy/SciPy.
records.hardware: CPU release; official changelog says a GPU-optimized implementation is in development, not available as this measured release.
records.inference: Forward moments and fitting interface; probabilistic sampling is composed externally.
records.public_status: PyPI source/wheel under proprietary noncommercial terms; redistribution is prohibited.
records.comparison_scope: The frozen Plummer tests use beta=beta_z=0, where the alignment distinction vanishes. Both fine-grid cases pass the declared accuracy gates; the coarse 45x9 intrinsic grid returns NaNs and is retained. Nonzero cylindrical anisotropy and JamPy's suggested approximation are different physical models. See the current JAM validation page for results and MGE limits.

records.geometry: Spherical and axisymmetric; cylindrical or spherical alignment
records.physics: Second-order Jeans with multi-Gaussian expansions (MGE), anisotropy, inclination and optional rotation prescriptions.
records.observables: Projected first/second velocity moments including proper motions; PSF and aperture treatment.
records.freedom: Flexible luminous/mass MGE components, M/L, black-hole mass and anisotropy.
records.solver: Direct integration of MGE Jeans expressions.
records.differentiation: No general physical-parameter autodiff interface documented in the inspected Python package.
records.hardware: Python/NumPy/SciPy CPU in the inspected implementation.
records.inference: Built-in fitting options; external Bayesian inference can wrap the forward model.
records.public_status: Source distributed through PyPI; package declares a proprietary license. Do not equate downloadability with an open-source license.
records.code_version: jampy 8.1.4; historical quadrature reference retained with original MGE coefficients
records.comparison_scope: Cylindrical alignment with the same target profiles approximated by MGE; report MGE residuals and fitting cost. Spherical-aligned JAM is a different closure.

records.target: Discrete stellar kinematics; original application to omega Centauri
records.physics: MGE tracer and mass; component anisotropy and rotation; inclination.
records.observables: Three first and six second velocity moments; the paper uses individual LOS/PM data with a contaminating population.
records.freedom: Separate tracer/mass MGEs, component mass scalings, anisotropy, rotation and optional black hole.
records.solver: Direct C/GSL integrations with an optional Python/Cython wrapper and interpolation grid.
records.differentiation: No physical-parameter automatic differentiation interface in the documented C implementation.
records.inference: Discrete likelihood framework in Watkins et al.; the public repository supplies the moment engine.
records.comparison_scope: Discrete stellar velocities, anisotropy, inclination and contamination are established precedents. They cannot individually establish JeansPy novelty. No new CJAM runtime measurement is reported.

records.target: Joint strong-lens imaging and spatially resolved stellar dynamics
records.physics: Composite lens mass and light models, MGE and spherical alignment; lensing and dynamics share mass parameters.
records.observables: Lensed image information and two-dimensional stellar second moments; paper combines several likelihood terms.
records.freedom: Flexible composite lens models, stellar/DM components and inclination; not the same tracer/closure as JeansPy's cylindrical model.
records.solver: Direct JAX rewrite of part of JAM with fixed integration grids; no learned surrogate for the dynamical solver described in the paper.
records.differentiation: JAX implementation is explicit. End-to-end physical-parameter gradient accuracy across the complete lensing/inference pipeline is not established by the inspected paper.
records.hardware: CPU/GPU hybrid; JAX matrix/integration work on GPU.
records.inference: Joint Bayesian modeling using emcee in the paper.
records.public_status: Paper publicly accessible; no public code repository was located in the inspected full text and cited software links. This is an access finding, not proof of non-public code.
records.code_version: No independently accessible GLaD code pin located
records.comparison_scope: Method/workflow comparison; not a numerically matched cylindrical Plummer+Zhao benchmark.

records.target: Stellar kinematic maps of strong-lens early-type galaxies
records.physics: Neural approximation to JAM maps for elliptical power-law total mass and Sersic light within a specified training distribution.
records.observables: Spatially resolved second-moment maps; intended for dynamical/lensing analyses.
records.freedom: Eight inputs in the published model: lens/mass scale and slope/flattening, light scale/index/flattening, anisotropy and inclination.
records.solver: Trained neural surrogate; training and weight provenance are part of the method.
records.differentiation: Differentiable learned mapping; existing differentiability precludes a novelty claim based only on autodiff.
records.hardware: GPU inference/training described; current README requires CUDA.
records.inference: Provides surrogate predictions and parameter sensitivities; compare the complete chosen external inference workflow explicitly.
records.public_status: Public code and separately downloadable weights; no license detected in GitHub metadata. Weight terms must be checked separately.
records.code_version: d941b6a049a40a6e1e901c2f221f08ac0b72f4d5; README announces updated weights on 2026-01-15, DOI 10.58119/ULG/WZFXYD
records.comparison_scope: Native in-domain model only. Plummer+Zhao dSphs do not match the published training family; no out-of-domain speed/accuracy claim.

records.target: General galactic dynamics and galaxy modeling
records.geometry: Spherical, axisymmetric and more general potentials/orbit models
records.physics: Potentials, forces, actions, distribution functions, DF moments, self-consistent and Schwarzschild models. Axisymmetric Jeans models are explicitly recorded in the May 2018 changelog.
records.observables: Positions/velocities, intrinsic/projected moments and model-dependent observables.
records.freedom: Broad potential, density and DF libraries; beyond a single Jeans closure.
records.solver: Direct C++ numerical dynamics with Python/Fortran interfaces.
records.differentiation: Spatial force/derivative interfaces exist; these are distinct from an end-to-end physical-parameter autodiff likelihood.
records.hardware: CPU C++ with parallel capabilities; no matching GPU Jeans path established here.
records.inference: Fitting framework and examples; inference target depends on the selected DF/model.
records.public_status: Public source; inspect the repository license terms rather than interpreting GitHub's NOASSERTION as a license.
records.code_version: Survey f302756b8af2b763db58e278e30478517dc8eea3; existing local submodule 4e62db6 (full pin in baseline git tree)
records.comparison_scope: Independent potential/DF-moment reference when assumptions agree. Rebuilding a DF each proposal measures that workflow, not a generic Jeans-solver limit.

records.target: General Galactic dynamics, potentials, orbits and DFs
records.geometry: General dynamics library; its jeans.py helpers assume spherical symmetry
records.physics: Spherical Jeans helper accepts tracer density and constant or radial anisotropy; sphericity of the supplied potential is not checked.
records.observables: sigmar and sigmalos return velocity dispersions; broader library supplies other dynamical observables.
records.freedom: Composable potentials, user-supplied density and anisotropy functions.
records.solver: Direct NumPy/SciPy Jeans integration; broader package includes C acceleration. Current source adds interpolation/refinement for radial moments.
records.differentiation: No JAX physical-parameter autodiff in the inspected Jeans helper.
records.hardware: CPU Python/C, depending on component; inspected Jeans integrations use SciPy.
records.inference: Forward helpers with external inference; general library also has fitting utilities.
records.code_version: Survey d243f989b61ec6398f46fafa49b886feac1134bf; pin the installed release separately for each measurement.
records.comparison_scope: Matched spherical density/potential/beta predictions after explicit unit conversion; fresh measurements needed for current optimized helper.

records.physics: Second-order Jeans with virial shape parameters (fourth-moment information), optional proper motions; current binulator release differs from the original free-form implementation.
records.observables: Binned photometry/velocity moments, virial shape constraints and optional PMs.
records.freedom: Flexible halo/anisotropy and tracer modeling; current public model choices must be specified.
records.differentiation: No physical-parameter autodiff interface documented in inspected code.
records.inference: binulator preprocessing then emcee-based mass modeling.
records.public_status: Public repository; no license detected in GitHub metadata.
records.paper_version: Read & Steger 2017, MNRAS 471, 4541; additional current-code citations listed in README
records.comparison_scope: Common second-moment forward subset versus native binned/VSP workflow separately; include preprocessing in native timing.

records.target: Spherical stellar systems from clusters to galaxies
records.physics: Second- and fourth-order Jeans equations with flexible anisotropy at both orders and non-Gaussian velocity PDF modeling.
records.observables: Individual LOS velocities and optional proper motions; photometric tracers may be unbinned.
records.freedom: Flexible mass/anisotropy/tracer models and higher-moment parameters.
records.solver: Direct higher-order numerical integration and velocity-PDF construction.
records.differentiation: No physical-parameter autodiff interface documented in inspected implementation.
records.code_version: Survey de56ee61b377608e63d4420f424def7ceaec942f; existing submodule 06d6a507 (full pin in baseline git tree)
records.paper_version: Banares-Hernandez, Read & Julio 2026, A&A 705, A212; arXiv:2509.24103v3 corrects equations 17, 18, 20, 23
records.comparison_scope: Second-moment subroutine only if inputs/definitions match; native non-Gaussian inference cannot be equated to JeansPy's Gaussian likelihood.

records.physics: Free-form density and anisotropy Jeans analysis with binned kinematics and virial shape information.
records.observables: Photometric/kinematic star inputs are preprocessed into moment constraints.
records.freedom: Nonparametric density description and flexible anisotropy/tracer parameters.
records.solver: Direct compiled extension via SWIG and Python orchestration.
records.inference: emcee wrapper with preprocessing and stored chains.
records.public_status: Public GPL-3.0 repository; README documents legacy dependency versions.
records.paper_version: Original GravSphere family; Genina et al. 2020, MNRAS 498, 144, plus relevant code-use citations
records.comparison_scope: Native free-form/VSP workflow is scientifically distinct. Previous installation failure is preliminary; any new failure requires its own log and environment.

records.physics: Parametric mass/anisotropy profiles and a chosen 3D velocity distribution (Gaussian in the founding paper). LOS projection generally gives a non-Gaussian velocity distribution.
records.observables: Unbinned projected phase space (R, v_los), including its radial selection.
records.freedom: Mass/tracer scale radii and anisotropy parameters; multiple tracer populations in public example.
records.solver: Direct integration of a projected phase-space model.
records.differentiation: No end-to-end physical-parameter autodiff documented in inspected repository.
records.hardware: CPU native code; build instructions use INSTALL.csh.
records.inference: Maximum-likelihood method in paper; repository includes MCMC output/test workflow.
records.public_status: Public GPL-3.0-or-later GitLab repository; no tags listed.
records.comparison_scope: Native phase-space likelihood comparison; not a matched Gaussian LOS likelihood without an explicit mathematical reduction.

records.target: Dark-matter annihilation/decay signals; dSph Jeans analysis
records.geometry: Spherical Jeans module; signal calculations also allow nonspherical halos/substructure
records.physics: Parametric Jeans mass modeling plus J/D integrals and particle/signal calculations; signal geometry is broader than Jeans geometry.
records.observables: Binned moments or individual velocities for Jeans fitting; J/D factors, fluxes and skymaps.
records.freedom: Selectable density/light/anisotropy models and halo/subhalo prescriptions.
records.solver: Direct C/C++ integration and statistical workflows.
records.differentiation: No physical-parameter autodiff interface documented in the inspected Jeans module.
records.hardware: CPU C/C++; dependencies vary by release and optional modules.
records.public_status: Public GitLab code; release-specific license/dependency terms apply.
records.code_version: Documentation v3.1.1; surveyed master 101aff8ecd2da20a71f7eb83fb6be2f8d4e99679; README warns master installation differs from release.
records.paper_version: Bonnivard et al. 2016 (Jeans module); Hutten, Combet & Maurin 2019, CPC 235, 336 (v3)
records.comparison_scope: Matched spherical moments or J/D geometry after explicit cuts/units; native all-sky/substructure signal work is outside JeansPy's scope.

records.geometry: Potential/orbit-dependent; not limited to spherical Jeans models
records.physics: Potential/force models, Hamiltonian orbits, coordinates and dynamical analysis.
records.observables: Trajectories and dynamical quantities; no complete matching dSph Jeans likelihood established in inspected API.
records.freedom: Composable potentials and flexible phase-space initial conditions.
records.differentiation: Spatial potential derivatives are supported; this does not establish JAX parameter gradients for a Jeans inference pipeline.
records.hardware: CPU Python/C implementation described by official documentation.
records.inference: Building blocks and examples for externally composed analyses.
records.comparison_scope: Scope and interoperability comparison; no invented Jeans timing or inference score.

records.physics: Unit-aware gravitational potentials, phase-space coordinates and orbit integration.
records.observables: Orbits and potential-derived quantities; a matching dSph Jeans likelihood was not located in the inspected surface.
records.solver: Direct JAX dynamics; no learned surrogate implied by JAX.
records.differentiation: Autodiff is an explicit project feature; comparison must distinguish its potential/orbit derivatives from the Jeans forward/likelihood tested here.
records.hardware: JAX CPU/GPU capability; actual device and precision require measurement.
records.inference: Composable differentiable primitives; no complete matching Jeans sampler established here.
records.public_status: Public MIT source; README says documentation is forthcoming.
records.paper_version: Repository citation; no primary methods paper located in README
records.comparison_scope: Scope and autodiff-context comparison; no fabricated Jeans benchmark.
